title: Conditional Compilation
hints: `#if` is decided at compile time; `#available` at runtime.
Use `#if swift(>=6.0)`, `#if os(macOS)`, `#if arch(arm64)`, `#if canImport(Foundation)`, `#if DEBUG`, then `if #available(macOS 13, *)`.
Each check appends one string to an array, in the order the statement lists.
jsBridge: `#if os(macOS)`, `#if swift(>=6)` and `#if DEBUG` are compile-time conditions, like build-time `process.env.NODE_ENV` checks that bundlers strip. `#available` is the **runtime** OS-version check.

compass.q: `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production')` is removed by bundlers. How is `#if DEBUG` similar, and different?
`#if os(iOS)` (compile-time) vs `if #available(iOS 17, *)` (runtime): when do you need each?
Code inside a false `#if` block: is it type-checked? Parsed?
Where do you use `#if DEBUG` in an app: mock data, logging, debug menus?
